source.title: Perception in real-time: predicting the present, reconstructing the past.

confidence_rationale: A published theoretical framework that is nearly isomorphic to ARC-129 plus MECH-501: predictive mechanisms extrapolate ahead to compensate for delays, and reconstruction mechanisms retroactively revise the represented timeline when predictions fail. Held at 0.45 because it is a review/proposal, it concerns perception rather than committed action, and it is independent convergence on the same idea rather than a test of it.
failure_signatures: Conceptual convergence can be mistaken for evidence; this paper proposes the mechanism, it does not demonstrate the discontinuity MECH-501 predicts.
Its 'reconstruction' revises the represented past (the timeline), whereas MECH-501 asserts replacement of the estimate consumed as 'now'; these may not be the same event.

mapping.source_claim_statement: At any moment perceptual mechanisms represent an entire timeline: prediction runs ahead to compensate for transmission delays, and reconstruction retroactively revises perception when those predictions do not come true.
mapping.ree_translation: Supplies an established name and literature home for MECH-501 (predict-then-reconstruct in real-time perception). It supports treating violation-triggered revision as a separate process from forward prediction, which is the claim's structural point.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Framework is about perceptual representation of external events under neural delay; it makes no claim about committed action, value-weighted surprise, or interaction with stopping/decommitment circuitry. It frames revision as rewriting the past segment of the timeline, which is related to but not identical with pulling the 'now' estimate back toward s_hat(t).
mapping.source_context: Trends in Cognitive Sciences opinion/review integrating flash-lag, motion extrapolation, EEG decoding and postdiction work.

confidence_components.notes: Theory paper; high conceptual fidelity to ARC-129/MECH-501, no new data.
